beliefs: Outer branch |x|>=2 has form f(x) = -sign(x)*A*|x|^p*exp(k*|x|) with A,p,k fit to positive-side magnitudes [E1, E7, E10, E15]
Outer branch is NOT exactly odd: negative side magnitudes are larger than positive side at moderate |x|, but converge to the same values at large |x| [E10, E12, E13, E14, E16]
At |x|>=~48 the two sides agree (f(-x)=-f(x)) to observed precision [E16]
Negative-side outer magnitudes exceed positive-side by a factor that decays from ~2.3 at |x|=2.5 to ~1 at |x|>=48 [E10, E14, E16]
f(2)=-60.2 and f(-2)=-67.0 exactly; outer law is only approximate near |x|=2 [E1, E4, E6]
On (0,1) f is exactly 0, with a sharp step to -4.3 at x=1.0 [E5, E9]
On (1,2) f rises smoothly from -4.3 toward ~-30 as x->2- [E3, E4, E5, E9]
On (-2,0) f is a smooth curve: ~+6 near -1, peaking ~+8 near -1.2, then dropping steeply to -67 at x=-2 [E3, E6]
Outer sign is negative for positive x, positive for negative x [E1, E7, E10, E14, E16]
Positive-side near-boundary magnitudes (2-4.5) are larger than the global log-linear fit predicts; a local correction factor applies [E15]
Negative-side near-boundary magnitudes (2-4.5) are larger still than positive side by a decaying ratio [E14]
notes: Fixed sign bug (outer was returning positive on positive side). Replaced odd assumption with a side-dependent magnitude: positive side uses log-linear fit plus near-boundary correction; negative side multiplies positive magnitude by a ratio r(|x|) that decays from ~2.3 at 2.5 to 1 at >=48, matching E14/E16.
